title: Two meanings of learning better
paragraphs: To ask whether sleep improves learning is already to compress several questions into one. Evidence that a memory survives an interval need not show that the learner has become more receptive to information not yet encountered. Nor would identifying a biological change, however persuasive as an explanation of one task, establish its relevance to another. A 2014 investigation of mice illustrates the distinction: following movement training, sleeping animals developed more new connections on particular branches of brain cells than animals kept awake. What remains unsettled is not the observation itself, but the distance over which an explanation may legitimately travel.

A human study published in 2025 exposes a related difficulty without resolving it. Across two experiments, sleep favoured recall of previously learned word pairs, whereas fresh pairs were learned without a corresponding advantage. Planned analyses did not establish the anticipated relationship between retention and subsequent learning. A further analysis, which took earlier recall into account, did suggest a relationship. To privilege that finding simply because it supplies a coherent story would reverse the appropriate burden of explanation: a result obtained after reconsidering the analysis requires investigation, rather than retrospectively making the original comparisons dispensable.

It would nevertheless be premature to treat the missing advantage as evidence that preserving memories cannot facilitate later learning. That conclusion would require the particular tasks to exhaust the relevant possibilities, an assumption these findings do not warrant. The converse shortcut is no safer: to describe retention and acquisition as aspects of memory does not make improvement in one sufficient evidence of improvement in the other. The studies are therefore neither rivals from which a reader must select a winner nor interchangeable demonstrations of a general benefit. Their contribution is conditional: each constrains an account of learning, provided the account retains the distinctions that make its supporting observations meaningful.

options.text: Research on sleep becomes persuasive when biological explanations take priority over behavioural results.

options.text: Each study can explain learning if its observations are translated into a common measure of improvement.
options.explanation: Cümle ortak bir ölçüye çevirme koşulu koymaz; gözlemlerin anlamını veren farklılıkları korumayı ister.

options.text: Each study limits the value of the others until their observations can be combined into one explanation.

options.text: Each study makes a provisional contribution because the observations need to be confirmed in another task.
options.explanation: Bu cümlede zorunlu koşul başka bir görevde doğrulama değildir; mevcut gözlemler arasındaki ayrımların açıklamada korunmasıdır.

options.text: Each study limits what an explanation can claim, provided the differences between observations are kept.

options.text: Failing to find an advantage in these tasks leaves open what a different task might show.

options.text: The adjusted analysis provides firmer grounds than the planned comparisons for predicting a future advantage.
